related_questions.question: Will an expired COVID test give a false positive?

text_blocks.snippet: An expired COVID-19 test is more likely to give a false negative result than a false positive. If an expired test shows a positive result, it is typically accurate, according to the Cleveland Clinic Newsroom. However, the opposite is true for a false negative, meaning an expired test may not detect the virus even if someone is infected.
snippet_highlighted_words: An expired COVID-19 test is more likely to give a false negative result than a false positive

text_blocks.snippet: Factors to consider when using an expired test:

list.snippet: Symptoms: If you have symptoms or have been exposed to someone with COVID-19, a positive result is more likely to be accurate.
Prior Infection: If you have had COVID-19 recently, it may be more likely that the test is picking up residual virus.
Test Type: Some tests are more reliable than others, even when expired.

text_blocks.snippet: It is generally recommended to use a test before its expiration date for the most accurate results. If you have concerns about the accuracy of an expired test, it's best to consult with a healthcare professional, according to www.health.com.
